source_refs.title: Manage unknown callers on iPhone - Apple Support
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; Phone app; conditions as stated on the page
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Within your Phone app and FaceTime settings, you get to decide who can reach you, and when.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Open Settings, tap Apps, then tap Phone. Choose how to handle calls from numbers not saved in your contacts. Scroll to Screen Unknown Callers and select one of three options. Never: Calls from unsaved numbers ring like any other call. Ask Reason for Calling: Calls are screened. The caller is asked why they're calling before your phone rings. Silence: Calls are silenced and sent to voicemail. Call screening may incur standard calling and data rates. On iOS versions earlier than iOS 17, Live Voicemail must also be turned on to use call screening. While roaming, calls are not screened, regardless of settings. If you call emergency services, call screening turns off for 24 hours.

source_refs.verified_excerpt: Missed calls and voicemails from unknown numbers go to an Unknown Callers list.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Open Settings, tap Apps, then tap Phone or FaceTime. Scroll to Call Filtering and turn on Unknown Callers. Missed calls and voicemails from unknown numbers go to an Unknown Callers list. To view that list, tap the Filter button. In the Phone app, the list appears under Recents in Classic view or Calls in Unified view.
